subject: No outputs when many values are included in qwindow function

messages.author: c2b608cf1a4e77a3
messages.subject: No outputs when many values are included in qwindow function
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am exploring time-segmented data in my current project. I keep GGIR running for days to analyze the current amount of data, and an alternative approach is to get hourly estimates of physical activity. With hour by hour data in part2_daysummary I can further aggregate estimates. However, GGIR is not generating outputs when many arguments are included in qwindow and mvpathreshold functions. 

I have tested some argument variations based on the examples described in Migueles JH and colleagues, 2019 (https://doi.org/10.1123/jmpb.2018-0063). The analysis runs fine with only one value in mvpathreshold and with qwindow=c(0,9,12,17,24). However, no files were generated when using the same qwindow argument but with two values in mvpathreshold. Based on my tests, the analysis runs fine with 10 qwindow values  and only one mvpathreshold value, or only three qwindow values for two  mvpathreshold values.

Any alternative to get this analysis to run?


This is the code I am trying to run to get hourly estimates.

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode=c(1,2), 
             datadir="D:/Simulations",  
             outputdir="D:/Simulations/Out",
             overwrite = TRUE,
             do.imp=TRUE,
             idloc=1,
             print.filename=TRUE,
             storefolderstructure = FALSE,  
             do.parallel = FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,
             do.lfenmo = TRUE, 
             do.enmoa = TRUE, 
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             do.en = TRUE, 
             do.bfen = TRUE, 
             do.hfen = TRUE, 
             do.hfenplus = TRUE,         
             chunksize=1, 
             printsummary=TRUE, 
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1, 
             hrs.del.start = 0,
             hrs.del.end = 0,  
             maxdur = 7, 
             includedaycrit = 16, 
             M5L5res = 10, 
             winhr = c(5,10), 
             qlevels = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9), 
             qwindow=c(seq(0,24,by=1)),  
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),  
             mvpathreshold =c(100.4, 200.6), 
             epochvalues2csv = TRUE, 
             IVIS_windowsize_minutes = 60,  
             IVIS_epochsize_seconds = 5,
             bout.metric=4)

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] No outputs when many values are included in qwindow function
parts:
This is something I fixed in the development version of GGIR a couple of weeks ago, which I intended to release as GGIR 2.0 via CRAN later this month or early May.

If you want to already try out the beta version of GGIR then please do:
install.packages("devtools")
install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "GGIR2.0") 

Note this is not a stable version yet, or in other words I am still editing it every week, but if you could try it and let me know if the warnings remain/disappear then that would be very helpful.

Thanks, Vincent

Thank you in advance

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] No outputs when many values are included in qwindow function
parts:
You are trying to use winhr =c(5,10) for windows of an hour. I suspect that this is where it goes wrong because finding the most or least active 5 or 10 hours in a 1 hour window is tricky. What happens if you replace it by winhr=c(0.25)?

Vincent

This is something I fixed in the development version of GGIR a couple of weeks ago, which I intended to release as GGIR 2.0 via CRAN later this month or early May.

If you want to already try out the beta version of GGIR then please do:
install.packages("devtools")
install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "GGIR2.0")
